tier_reason: First-party numbers posted by the author (Robert Clausecker) in his own Phabricator review D45670, comparing the asm kernels against libmd's old and new C MD5 block functions on two named CPUs; no compiler, flags, input size or benchmark command are visible, and the review page itself is unreachable here (reviews.freebsd.org ENOTFOUND), so the figures are confirmed from WebSearch snippets only. Kernel code is public (lib/libmd/amd64/md5block.S, md5dispatch.c) but no benchmark harness is, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Snippet only (review page unreachable here): Ryzen 7 PRO 7840U (Zen 4): orig 774.6 MB/s, generic 758.5, baseline asm 945.5, bmi1 asm 1062.4, avx512 asm 936.0 (derived from snippet data: bmi1 1.40x over generic C, 1.37x over orig C; baseline asm 1.22x over orig). Core i7-1165G7 (Tiger Lake): orig 605.9 MB/s, generic 587.8, baseline asm 765.3, bmi1 854.0, avx512 965.1 (derived from snippet data: avx512 1.64x over generic C, 1.59x over orig C). The ifunc dispatcher picks bmi1 on AMD and avx512 on Intel parts with AVX-512F/VL, matching the fastest variant per CPU.
corrections.caveats: The commit d92e987 ('lib/libmd: import md5 amd64 kernels', committed 2025-10-24, Reviewed by imp, Approved by markj) carries no numbers, only 'Differential Revision: https://reviews.freebsd.org/D45670'. reviews.freebsd.org, reviews-dev.freebsd.org and cgit.freebsd.org do not resolve here, so every number comes from WebSearch result snippets of the D45670 review (titled 'lib/libmd: reimplement and enhance md5', opened by fuz on 2024-06-21) and is snippet only. One search snippet notes that an earlier revision of the review (id=144760) carried different labels and numbers, so the figures may predate later changes to the committed kernels; a related review (D52909) snippet mentions a Zen 4 performance regression noticed when moving the md5 code. Compiler, flags, input size and command are unknown; author-run on two laptop CPUs, one run each as far as visible. 'orig' is the previous md5c.c and 'generic' the reimplemented C path, so the baseline is libmd's own C code, not OpenSSL MD5. The author notes the AVX-512 kernel is not really vectorised (it uses vpternlogd for the round functions), and md5dispatch.c skips it on AMD because it 'performs poorly on AMD'. The kernel build always uses the generic C version (the AVX-512 kernel is compiled only outside _KERNEL).

notes: Real, copyable BSD-2-Clause asm MD5 kernels in FreeBSD libmd with a modest 1.4-1.6x gain over the C block function; numbers confirmed only through search snippets of the blocked Phabricator review, with the Tiger Lake 'orig' figure now exact (605.9 MB/s). Shortcomings: snippet-only evidence, no published harness, compiler or flags, baseline is libmd's own C code rather than OpenSSL, numbers may come from an earlier review revision.
